fields.name: Position
fields.evidence: 16-byte block copied whole as four dwords by bg3.exe+0x2D605A0 (~ esv::ChasmSystem::UpdateNewChasmEntities: component stride 0x30, 'local_3b8 = *puVar17 .. puVar17[3]') and passed beside a second block of the same shape that the code builds as {translate of ls::TransformComponent (12 bytes), byte +0xC = 1} - an optional position with its has-value byte at +0xC. Live samples (9, bg3_dx11): when byte +0xC is 1, +0/+4/+8 are ordinary floats (268.75, 42.8, 10.25 ...); when it is 0 the 12 bytes hold stale data (heap-like values) - the disengaged storage. Byte +0xD (0/1/2) is padding of the optional. The source of the request, Toolkit esv::ChasmSystem::LEGACY_EntityEnteredChasm, takes an ls::Optional<Vector3f>. Name inferred.

fields.name: Cause
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2D605A0 passes puVar17 + 4 (+0x10) as an entity to the event listeners and to bg3.exe+0x3090370; Toolkit UpdateNewChasmEntities passes &+0x10 as the second entity of StoryGameEventManager::ThrowEnteredChasm, whose Osiris event is EnteredChasm(_Object, _Cause, _Chasm, _fallbackPos...): the name is the Osiris parameter. Live: entity handles or the null handle 0xFFC0000000000000.

fields.name: Chasm
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2D605A0 passes puVar17 + 6 (+0x18) as a Guid to bg3.exe+0x3009350 (fallback position in the chasm area; Toolkit: only user of 'Chasm trigger with GUID %s is not found') and converts it to an entity (bg3.exe+0x1013470) for the event; ProcessSavegameLoaded bg3.exe+0x2D5DD90 reads the four dwords +0x18..+0x24 of a 0x30-stride component and tests them for zero. Converted to the _Chasm entity of the Osiris event EnteredChasm. Live: random-looking 16 bytes.

fields.name: FallbackTimer
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2D605A0: 'if (puVar17[10] == -1) { ... puVar17[10] = 10; }' (+0x28). Toolkit esv::ChasmSystem::UpdateStoryFallbackTimer decrements it while > 0 and calls LEGACY_EnterChasmHandled at 0. Live: always 0xFFFFFFFF.

fields.name: StoryActionId
fields.evidence: Toolkit UpdateHandledRequests copies these 4 bytes into an optional of a request (has-value byte 1 beside it); LEGACY_EntityEnteredChasm, the entry point that queues chasm entries, takes ls::TypeWrap<unsigned int, eoc::TStoryActionIDClassname> - the only 4-byte argument. Live (bg3_dx11): small integers 0, 0x21, 0xBF, 0xDF, 0xE0, 0xEC, 0xF7, 0x100 with the upper bytes zero - 4-byte width; the name follows that argument.
